$comment: Usage documentation for every token. Consumed by build.mjs, which validates coverage against the token tree and emits CSS comments, JSDoc, TOKENS.md, and dist/usage.json. Edit this file — never the generated output.
rules: Never use a raw palette token (color.neutral.*, color.accent.*, color.success.*, color.warning.*, color.danger.*, color.white, color.black) in a component. They are identical in both themes, so a component using one is broken in the other. Use a theme.* semantic token instead. color.data.* is the one exception — it exists for direct use in data visualization.

Every color decision has exactly one correct semantic token. If none of them fits, the component needs a new semantic token added to both semantics/theme/light.json and semantics/theme/dark.json via the design-tokens skill — do not reach into the palette.
Backgrounds come from theme.bg.* or a role's bg/subtle. Text and icons come from theme.fg.* or a role's fg. Never put a role's bg behind text unless a pairing below allows it.
Reference tokens as CSS variables (var(--ds-<path-with-dashes>)), not as literal values. theme.accent-role.bg is var(--ds-theme-accent-role-bg).

Use the space scale for every margin, padding, and gap. Never write an arbitrary pixel value; pick the nearest step, or the rolled-up gap/stack/padding/page/control role that already names the situation.

Interactive controls get their height from size.control.*, their hover/press feedback from the .ds-state-layer class (not from hand-written hover colors), their focus ring from focus.* plus theme.focus-ring, and validation/selection emphasis from a role's ring (an inset stroke, not the focus outline).
theme.* is the only family whose value differs between light and dark. Everything under src/primitives/*.json is theme-independent, including color.data.*.
aria-disabled, not the disabled attribute, on interactive primitives — the control stays focusable and screen-reader discoverable, styled with state.disabled-opacity.

color.summary: Raw hue ramps (neutral/accent/success/warning/danger, 50 → 950) sourced from the underlying design system. Theme-independent — do not use directly in a component.
use: Only as a reference target inside semantics/theme/light.json and semantics/theme/dark.json.
dont: Direct use in components — these values are identical in both themes, so a component using them is unreadable in one of them.

instead.Role fill, text, or tint: theme.accent-role.bg, theme.success-role.bg, theme.warning-role.bg, or theme.danger-role.bg (and each role's .fg / .subtle)

scale.400-500: Low-emphasis text; the midpoint that reads acceptably on both light and dark backgrounds.
scale.600-700: Secondary text and role fills in light theme; borders in dark theme.
scale.800-950: Primary text in light theme; backgrounds and role subtles in dark theme.

color.data.summary: Data-visualization palette — a categorical set for series identity, plus five-step sequential ramps per hue. The one palette group meant for direct use.
use: Chart series colors: color.data.categorical.* for discrete series, in the listed order, cycling if you run out.
A single-hue sequential ramp (color.data.blue, .teal, .orange, …) for a magnitude scale within one series.
color.data.neutral for a de-emphasized or 'other' series.
dont: UI chrome — buttons, backgrounds, text, borders. Use theme.* for all of that.
Assigning meaning by index alone across unrelated charts — keep a series-to-color mapping consistent within one view.
notes: Unlike every other palette group, these values are picked directly, not routed through a theme role — a chart's legend is not the same design problem as a button's background.

theme.bg.canvas.summary: The page's own background, behind every surface.
use: The <body> background.
Any full-bleed region that is not itself a raised surface.
dont: Card, dialog, menu, or dropdown backgrounds — those are theme.bg.surface, one step up so they read as raised.

theme.bg.surface.summary: A raised surface sitting on top of the canvas — the default background for any container with an edge.
use: Card, dialog, menu, popover, and dropdown backgrounds.
The default (unfilled) button background.
dont: The page background itself — that is theme.bg.canvas.

theme.bg.subtle.summary: A quiet, faintly recessed or striped background — one step of emphasis below a surface, without reading as an interactive control.
use: Table header rows and zebra stripes.
A quiet section band inside a surface.
dont: An interactive hover/press background — use .ds-state-layer instead of a static fill.

theme.bg.muted.summary: The most recessed background — an inset well, a track, or a skeleton-loading placeholder.
use: A progress track behind its filled bar.
A skeleton-loading block.
An inset search field or well.

instead.Body text on this background: theme.fg.secondary, not theme.fg.muted, which falls to AA-large here

theme.fg.primary.summary: The default, highest-emphasis text and icon color.
use: Body copy, headings, and meaningful (non-decorative) icons.

theme.fg.secondary.summary: Lower-emphasis text — supporting copy that should not compete with primary content.
use: Helper text, captions, timestamps, metadata.

theme.fg.muted.summary: The lowest-emphasis foreground — placeholders and decorative icons only.
dont: Body-size text on theme.bg.muted — falls to AA-large only there; use theme.fg.secondary for readable body text on that background.
use: Input placeholder text.
A decorative icon that carries no meaning on its own.

theme.fg.on-accent.summary: White text/icon color for use on a filled, saturated role background.
use: Label on a primary (accent) or destructive (danger) button.
Icon on a filled accent or danger badge.
dont: On theme.success-role.bg or theme.warning-role.bg — both are known contrast gaps (see Known gaps). Use the role's subtle/fg pairing for text instead.

theme.border.default.summary: The standard, low-contrast divider and card outline.
use: Card/panel outline.
A divider between list rows or sections.

theme.border.strong.summary: A higher-contrast border for elements that need to read as interactive or as a boundary the eye should stop at.
use: Text input and select borders.
The outlined (secondary) button border.

theme.accent-role.bg.summary: Filled accent background for the single highest-priority action in a view.
use: Primary button background.
Selected state of a toggle, tab indicator, or segmented control.
Filled accent badge, or the filled portion of a progress bar.
dont: More than one action per view — a screen with two primary buttons has no primary button.
Large background regions; it is a control fill, not a page color.
Behind theme.fg.primary or theme.fg.secondary — the only foreground permitted here is theme.fg.on-accent.

instead.A second, lower-priority action: theme.bg.surface with theme.border.strong (secondary button), or theme.secondary-role.bg

theme.accent-role.fg.summary: Accent-colored text for a link or a text-only action.
use: Inline link color.
The tertiary/text button variant's label.
Icon or text on an accent-role.subtle background.

theme.accent-role.subtle.summary: A tinted, low-saturation accent background that carries text safely.
use: Informational banner background (paired with theme.accent-role.fg text).
A selected menu item or nav item's background.
dont: As a substitute for theme.accent-role.bg on a primary action — this is a tint, not a fill.

theme.accent-role.ring.summary: Inset accent stroke marking a selected or actively-validating control — distinct from the keyboard focus ring.
use: A checked/selected input's inset outline, alongside its own background/border.
An in-progress validation state on a field (e.g. while checking availability).
dont: As a replacement for the :focus-visible outline (theme.focus-ring) — the two can coexist but answer different questions (keyboard focus vs. selection/validation state).

theme.secondary-role.bg.summary: Background for the secondary (outlined) button and similar lower-priority filled controls.
use: Secondary button background — paired with theme.secondary-role.border and theme.secondary-role.fg.

theme.secondary-role.fg.summary: Text/icon color for content on theme.secondary-role.bg.

theme.secondary-role.border.summary: Border for the secondary (outlined) button and similar controls.
use: Secondary button border.

theme.tertiary-role.fg.summary: Text color for the lowest-emphasis (tertiary/text) button variant — same hue as accent-role.fg, kept as its own role so a future rebrand can diverge them.
use: The tertiary button's label color.

theme.success-role.bg.summary: Saturated success fill — a non-text indicator color, not a text background.
use: A status dot, chip fill, or progress-bar segment indicating success.
dont: Behind any text, including theme.fg.on-accent — known contrast gap. Use theme.success-role.subtle with theme.success-role.fg for a success message instead.

theme.success-role.fg.summary: Success-colored text for messages and icons.
use: Success banner/message text.
A success icon.

theme.success-role.subtle.summary: Tinted success background that safely carries text.
use: Success banner/message background, paired with theme.success-role.fg.

theme.success-role.ring.summary: Inset success stroke for a control that just passed validation.
use: A field's inset outline after a successful validation check.

theme.warning-role.bg.summary: Saturated warning fill — a non-text indicator color, not a text background.
use: A status dot, chip fill, or progress-bar segment indicating warning.
dont: Behind any text — known contrast gap even for large text. Use theme.warning-role.subtle with theme.warning-role.fg for a warning message.

theme.warning-role.fg.summary: Warning-colored text for messages and icons.

theme.warning-role.subtle.summary: Tinted warning background that safely carries text.
use: Warning banner/message background, paired with theme.warning-role.fg.

theme.warning-role.ring.summary: Inset warning stroke for a control with an unresolved caution state.
use: A field's inset outline when a value is valid but risky (e.g. approaching a limit).

theme.danger-role.bg.summary: Filled danger background for a destructive action.
use: Destructive button background (paired with theme.fg.on-accent text).
A status dot or chip fill indicating an error state.

instead.An error message with text at any size: theme.danger-role.subtle background with theme.danger-role.fg text (theme.danger-role.subtle with theme.fg.on-accent falls to AA-large in light — see Known gaps)

theme.danger-role.fg.summary: Danger-colored text for validation errors and error messages.
use: Field validation error text.
Error banner/message text and icon.

theme.danger-role.subtle.summary: Tinted danger background that carries text at large sizes; use theme.fg.primary rather than theme.fg.on-accent for body-size text here.
use: Error banner/message background, paired with theme.danger-role.fg.

theme.danger-role.ring.summary: Inset danger stroke for a control that failed validation.
use: A field's inset outline after a failed validation check.

theme.focus-ring.summary: The keyboard focus indicator color, always used with focus.ring-width and focus.ring-offset.
use: outline-color in a :focus-visible rule, on every interactive element.
dont: Removing the ring, or reusing this color for anything that isn't a focus indicator.

example.css: :focus-visible { outline: var(--ds-focus-ring-width) solid var(--ds-theme-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--ds-focus-ring-offset); }

theme.elevation.raised.summary: Shadow for content that is part of the page but sits slightly above it.
use: Resting cards and panels.

theme.elevation.overlay.summary: Shadow for a transient surface anchored to a trigger.
use: Dropdowns, menus, popovers, tooltips.

theme.elevation.modal.summary: Shadow for a surface that takes over the screen.
use: Dialogs, drawers, sheets.

border.summary: Border widths — a raw px scale, plus a semantic default step.
use: border-width, or a component's default border shorthand via border.default.

scale.2: Emphasis border, e.g. a focus ring's outline-width.
scale.3: The focus ring's outline-offset, borrowed here so ring geometry stays on this same scale.
scale.default: 1px — border.1. The width for theme.border.default / theme.border.strong.

elevation.summary: Box-shadow scale expressing how far a surface floats above the page. Height encodes how temporary a surface is. Each step has a '-strong' twin with a darker shadow, used in the dark theme where a shadow this soft would be nearly invisible.
use: box-shadow on a raised surface, via the theme.elevation.* role that names the situation — never this scale directly.
dont: Reaching for elevation.low/med/high directly in component CSS — use theme.elevation.raised/overlay/modal so the dark-theme '-strong' swap happens automatically.

scale.low: Resting cards and panels — content that is part of the page. Light-theme value of theme.elevation.raised.
scale.med: Dropdowns, menus, popovers, tooltips — transient surfaces anchored to a trigger. Light-theme value of theme.elevation.overlay.
scale.high: Dialogs, drawers, sheets — surfaces that take over the screen. Light-theme value of theme.elevation.modal.

ring.summary: Inset box-shadow scale for validation/selection strokes, one per role plus a neutral pair. Always reached via a role's theme.*-role.ring, never directly.
use: The value behind theme.accent-role.ring, theme.success-role.ring, theme.warning-role.ring, and theme.danger-role.ring.
dont: Using ring.* directly in component CSS instead of the theme role — the role is what varies by (future) theme; the raw ring color does not need to today, but routing through the role keeps every consumer on one lookup path.
Using a ring in place of the keyboard focus outline (theme.focus-ring) — rings mark selection/validation state, not keyboard focus.

scale.neutral: An unfocused/unvalidated inset stroke, for a control that needs a resting inset outline without implying a role.

opacity.summary: Raw opacity values behind the state scale. Do not use directly — use state.*-opacity.
dont: Direct use in components.

state.summary: Interaction-state opacities, composed by the .ds-state-layer class — do not write hand-rolled hover/press rules.
use: Automatically applied by adding the ds-state-layer class alongside a component's own class.
state.disabled-opacity directly, on an aria-disabled element.
dont: A new :hover/:active background-color rule — compose .ds-state-layer instead.

focus.summary: Focus-ring geometry. Always used together with theme.focus-ring.
use: outline-width and outline-offset in a :focus-visible rule.
dont: Removing the ring or shrinking it below these values.
Setting the offset to 0 on a filled accent control — the gap is what separates the ring from the accent fill behind it.

scale.ring-width: The outline thickness, thick enough to see at a glance.
scale.ring-offset: The gap between the element and the ring, which keeps the ring legible against a filled background.

example.css: :focus-visible { outline: var(--ds-focus-ring-width) solid var(--ds-theme-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--ds-focus-ring-offset); }

use: height (and usually min-width) of buttons, inputs, and other controls, via size.control.*.

scale.control.sm: Compact control height, e.g. a dense table's inline actions.
scale.control.md: The default control height for buttons and inputs.

space.summary: The spacing scale, plus rolled-up roles (gap/stack/padding/control/page/section) that name a specific spacing situation instead of a raw step.
use: Every margin, padding, and gap — prefer the matching role (space.gap.md, space.page.gutter, …) over a raw step when one names the situation.
dont: An arbitrary pixel value anywhere spacing is needed.

scale.gap.xs: Tightest inline gap, e.g. an icon and its label.
scale.gap.md: The default gap between related inline items.
scale.gap.lg: A looser gap between grouped inline items.
scale.stack.xs: Tightest vertical rhythm, e.g. a label and its helper text.
scale.stack.sm: Compact vertical rhythm within a component.
scale.stack.md: The default vertical gap between stacked elements.
scale.stack.lg: A looser vertical gap between sections of one component.
scale.section: Vertical gap between major page sections.
scale.control.padding-inline.sm: Horizontal padding for a size.control.sm control.
scale.control.padding-inline.md: Horizontal padding for a size.control.md control.
scale.control.padding-inline.lg: Horizontal padding for a size.control.lg control.
scale.page.block-start: Vertical padding above a page's first section.
scale.page.block-end: Vertical padding below a page's last section.

radius.summary: Corner radius, plus rolled-up roles that name a specific surface's radius.
use: border-radius — prefer the matching role (radius.element, radius.container, …) over a raw step when one names the situation.

scale.sm: Smallest usable radius — a chip or tag.
scale.xl: A large surface's radius, e.g. a bottom sheet.
scale.2xl: The largest fixed radius, for full-page surfaces.
scale.inner: radius.sm — an element nested inside an already-rounded container.
scale.element: radius.md — the default control radius, named for reuse in recipes.
scale.chat: radius.xl — a chat bubble or similarly large rounded surface.
scale.page: radius.2xl — a full-page or sheet-level surface.
scale.pill: radius.full — a pill-shaped control or badge.

font.summary: Raw typography primitives (family, size steps, weight steps, line-height steps, letter-spacing steps). Do not use directly — use the type.* semantic scale, which is built from these.
dont: Direct use of font.size.*, font.weight.*, or font.line-height.* in component CSS — use type.* instead, which names the role (body, heading, label, control) rather than a raw step.

instead.Any text sizing decision: type.size.base, type.body.size, type.heading.size, type.label.size, or type.control.size.md

scale.family.mono: Monospace, for code and tabular figures.
scale.weight.bold: Emphasis weight — headings, labels, and button text.
scale.line-height.350: A looser fixed line-height, for a large control.
scale.letter-spacing.tightest: Tightest tracking, for the largest display text.
scale.letter-spacing.wide: Slightly open tracking, used by type.label for its uppercase treatment.

type.summary: The usable typography scale — role-based (body, heading, label, control) and a raw size scale, both built from font.*.
use: type.body.* for paragraph and default UI text.
type.heading.* for section/card headings.
type.label.* for uppercase eyebrow labels and form field labels.
type.control.size/.line-height/.weight for text inside a size.control.* sized control.
type.size.* when you need a raw size off the T-shirt scale without the rest of a role's styling.
dont: Reaching into font.size.* or font.weight.* directly — always go through type.*.

scale.label.letter-spacing: Tracking for the label role's uppercase treatment.
scale.label.text-transform: Always uppercase for the label role.
scale.control.size.sm: Text size inside a size.control.sm control.
scale.control.size.md: Text size inside a size.control.md control.
scale.control.size.lg: Text size inside a size.control.lg control.
scale.tracking.display-1: Tightest tracking, for type.size.5xl-scale display text.
scale.tracking.display-2: Very tight tracking, for large display text.
scale.tracking.signal-1: Open tracking, for small all-caps signal text.

motion.summary: Duration and easing primitives, plus rolled-up roles that name a specific transition situation.
use: transition-duration / transition-timing-function, via a role (motion.interactive.*, motion.overlay.*, motion.modal.*) rather than a raw duration when one names the situation.

scale.duration.fast: Backing value for motion.interactive — hover/press feedback, toggles.
scale.duration.fast-max: Upper bound of the fast band.
scale.duration.medium-min: Lower bound of the medium band.
scale.duration.medium: Backing value for motion.overlay — menus, popovers, tooltips entering/leaving.
scale.duration.medium-max: Upper bound of the medium band.
scale.duration.slow-min: Lower bound of the slow band.
scale.duration.slow: Backing value for motion.modal — dialogs, sheets, drawers.
scale.duration.spin-reduced: A slowed spinner rotation for prefers-reduced-motion.
scale.easing.standard: The default curve for most transitions.

pairings.note: Large text and non-text only. For body-size text on theme.bg.muted use theme.fg.secondary.
Large text and icons only on this background in the light theme. Use theme.fg.primary for body-size text on theme.danger-role.subtle.

knownGaps.note: theme.success-role.bg is a non-text indicator color in both themes.
knownGaps.workaround: Put success text on theme.success-role.subtle using theme.success-role.fg.

knownGaps.note: theme.warning-role.bg is the lightest role fill and carries no text at any size.
knownGaps.workaround: Put warning text on theme.warning-role.subtle using theme.warning-role.fg.

knownGaps.note: theme.fg.on-accent is white; theme.danger-role.subtle is a light tint in the light theme, so white text disappears on it.
knownGaps.workaround: Use theme.danger-role.fg for text on theme.danger-role.subtle, or theme.fg.on-accent only on theme.danger-role.bg.

button-primary.summary: The single highest-priority action in a view.

tokens.hover/press: compose the .ds-state-layer class — do not swap the background

button-secondary.summary: A supporting action shown next to a primary one.

button-destructive.summary: An action that deletes or revokes something.

text-field.summary: A single-line input with a label, helper text, and validation states.

notice.summary: An inline banner. Only the tinted subtle backgrounds carry text; the saturated role fills do not.

tokens.leading accent bar (optional): the matching role bg — a non-text use

dialog.summary: A modal surface that takes over the screen.

menu.summary: A transient list of actions anchored to a trigger.
